title: A Very Strong El Niño Could Change Weather Around the World
summary:
Weather experts say Earth could have the strongest El Niño ever recorded this year. Some people call it "Super El Niño," NPR reports.

El Niño is a natural pattern that happens every two to seven years. It starts when a big area of ocean water near the equator in the Pacific gets warm. That warm water heats the air and changes weather around the world.

Scientist Daniel Vimont says it is like dropping a giant rock into a pond. Even places far away feel the waves.

Forecasters at NOAA, a U.S. weather agency, call this one "very strong." Ocean water in one key area is more than 2 degrees Celsius warmer than normal. They think it will last into early 2027.

In the United States, southern states often get more rain during El Niño. That can cause floods, but it can also help dry places get water. Northern states are often warmer and drier.
why_it_matters: El Niño can change rain and temperatures where people live, so knowing about it helps families and communities prepare.
